msItem.title: Collectio decem partium (expansion of Ivo of Chartres, Panormia)
msItem.note: This is seemingly a revised version of the Panormia, by an unknown author, made about 1130, and is described by M. Paul Fournier as “Collection en dix parties', see Les Collections Canoniques attribuées à Yves de Chartres, Bibliothèque de l'École des Chartes (1897), p. 147.

provenance.orgName: Canterbury, Kent. Benedictine abbey of St Augustine (originally of St Peter and St Paul)
provenance.p: For evidence that the manuscript was written at St Augustine's, see T. A. M. Bishop, 'Notes on Cambridge Manuscripts', Transactions of the Cambridge Bibliographical Society, 1 (1953), pp. 432-41 at p. 438.

provenance.orgName: Canterbury, Kent. Benedictine cathedral priory of Holy Trinity or Christ Church
provenance.p: This attribution has a complex evolution within Medieval Libraries of Great Britain. It was accepted with a query in the first edition (1941), with the following footnote: Sixteenth-century notes wrongly connect these volumes with Archbishop Theodore of Canterbury. Cf. M. R. James, in The Library, vii (1927), 330. Conversely, in the second edition (1964), the attribution was rejected (with no further comment). There were no relevant changes in the Supplement (1987). During MLGB3 (2010-2015), the attribution was accepted with a query, with the following evidence provided: From Christ Church, canterbury. No mark remains, but the evidence of the script is strong; cf. also Parker's note on fol. 1r, which suggests a connexion with Canterbury. Although no citation was given for this evidence, the sentence is loosely paraphrased from M. R. James, A descriptive catalogue of the manuscripts in the library of Corpus Christi College, volume 1 (Cambridge, 1912), p. 182.

recordHist.source: Neil R. Ker, ed., Medieval Libraries of Great Britain: A List of Surviving Books, Royal Historical Society Guides and Handbooks, 3 (London, 1941; 2nd edn, 1964; supplement, ed. Andrew G. Watson, 1987; digital edn, ed. Richard Sharpe and James M. W. Willoughby, 2010–15).

revisionDesc.change: Record edited (Sian Witherden) to clarify data history with respect to Canterbury Christ Church attribution.
